tagline: Cool mountain air, the Phu Kradueng sea of fog, and the Phi Ta Khon festival in Dan Sai
introHtml: Loei is an Isan province that doesn't look like the rest of Isan, because it's full of high mountains and some of the coldest weather in the country. When people think of Loei they picture Phu Kradueng, where you climb all day to reach the top, Phu Ruea, where winter nights get cold enough to turn dew into frost, and Chiang Khan, which has become a popular riverside walking street along the Mekong. On the cultural side there's the Phi Ta Khon festival in Dan Sai, which you won't see anywhere else. For food there's down-to-earth Isan cooking plus local favourites like khai kratha and Chiang Khan's crystal coconut. Come to Loei and you can hike up a mountain, wander a Mekong town, and take some cool weather home with you.
bestTime: November–February is the coldest, with the sea of fog rolling in often at both Phu Ruea and Phu Thok. Phu Kradueng is open for climbing from October to May, and the Phi Ta Khon festival runs around June–July.

highlights.name: Phu Kradueng
highlights.blurb: A flat-topped mountain that takes a climb of over 5 kilometres to reach the plateau. Up top there are wide grasslands, waterfalls, and a sunrise spot at Pha Nok Aen. It's a dream peak for hikers.

highlights.name: Chiang Khan
highlights.blurb: An old town on the Mekong with a wooden-house walking street, cafes, and guesthouses lined up along the river. Waking early to give sticky-rice alms along the riverside road is the signature image of this place.

highlights.name: Phu Ruea
highlights.blurb: A peak that gets cold enough in winter to form frost, known locally as mae kha ning. It has sea-of-fog and sunrise viewpoints where people camp out overnight to wait for the cold.

highlights.name: Phi Ta Khon, Dan Sai
highlights.blurb: A merit-making festival where the people of Dan Sai put on brightly coloured ghost masks and parade through town. It's a local tradition you won't find anywhere else.

highlights.name: Kaeng Khut Khu
highlights.blurb: A rocky rapid in the middle of the Mekong near Chiang Khan. In the dry season the water drops and the rocks show clearly, with riverside restaurants and crystal coconut sold as souvenirs.

highlights.name: Phu Thok and Phra That Si Song Rak
highlights.blurb: Phu Thok is an easy-to-reach sea-of-fog viewpoint near Chiang Khan, while Phra That Si Song Rak in Dan Sai is an old, revered stupa that the people of Loei hold dear.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, laap, koi, grilled chicken, and bold bamboo-shoot soup are found all over the province. It's the everyday, home-style meal for locals in Loei.

foodScene.name: Khai kratha, Chiang Khan
foodScene.note: The classic Chiang Khan breakfast: a hot pan of eggs with mu yo and Chinese sausage, eaten with bread for dipping. Having it along the riverside road in the morning comes with the atmosphere.

foodScene.name: Crystal coconut and Chiang Khan souvenirs
foodScene.note: Sweet, crunchy candied coconut is the number-one souvenir of Chiang Khan and Kaeng Khut Khu, in white and other colours, and easy to take home.

foodScene.name: Mekong river fish
foodScene.note: Riverside spots around Chiang Khan and Kaeng Khut Khu serve grilled fish, steamed fish, and tom yum made with fish from the Mekong, eaten in the breeze by the water.

foodScene.name: Chiang Khan cafes and coffee
foodScene.note: The Chiang Khan walking street is full of cafes in old wooden houses. You can sip coffee with a river view or shoot photos of the old-town corners all day.

foodScene.name: Foraged greens and local vegetables
foodScene.note: In the rainy season the mountain districts bring mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and local greens to the markets, used in curries and with chilli dips the way mountain folk eat.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: A popular dinner in the town and in Phu Ruea, eaten warm to match the cold weather, especially in winter.

foodScene.name: Chiang Khan walking-street street food
foodScene.note: In the evening the walking street has grilled and fried snacks, local sweets, and nibbles to graze on the whole way down.

attractions.name: Phu Kradueng National Park
attractions.blurb: A flat-topped mountain you climb all day on your own. Up top there are grasslands, waterfalls, and a sunrise spot at Pha Nok Aen. It's a goal for hikers.

attractions.name: Chiang Khan
attractions.blurb: An old town on the Mekong with a wooden-house walking street, cafes, and places to stay. Waking early for sticky-rice alms along the riverside comes with the atmosphere.

attractions.name: Phu Ruea National Park
attractions.blurb: A peak with bitterly cold weather that forms frost in winter. It has sea-of-fog and sunrise viewpoints, and people like to camp out to wait for the cold.

attractions.name: Phra That Si Song Rak
attractions.blurb: An old stupa in Dan Sai, built as a symbol of friendship. It's revered by the people of Loei and has an annual celebration.

attractions.name: Kaeng Khut Khu
attractions.blurb: A rocky rapid in the middle of the Mekong near Chiang Khan. In the dry season the water drops and the rocks show clearly, with riverside restaurants and crystal coconut souvenirs.

attractions.name: Phu Thok
attractions.blurb: A sea-of-fog viewpoint near Chiang Khan that's easy to reach by songthaew. Wake early and you'll find white fog drifting over the Mekong and the town.

attractions.name: Wat Neramit Wipatsana, Dan Sai
attractions.blurb: A temple built entirely from orange laterite, set on a rise near Phra That Si Song Rak. You can walk around and admire the stucco work and murals.

attractions.name: Suan Hin Pha Ngam (Kunming of Loei)
attractions.blurb: A cluster of sharp limestone formations standing in rows like the stone forest of Kunming. You can wind your way along paths between the rocks and take in the unusual views.
